rationale: Cloud architects and platform engineers at mid-market companies deploying LLMs on Azure are real business buyers with infrastructure budgets, and pricing confusion around AI gateway tiers is a concrete decision-blocker that costs real money if misjudged. Adjacent tools (Infracost, CloudHealth) confirm this segment pays for cost clarity tooling. Buildability and autonomy are strong — a Claude-powered pricing explainer and cost calculator is highly automatable and deliverable as a self-serve web tool. However, the market is somewhat narrow (Azure-specific AI Gateway buyers), lead reachability requires finding engineers actively in the Azure AI evaluation phase (harder than a directory), and no responsiveness data exists. Sits exactly at the validate floor — worth a lightweight test but not enough signal to invest in building without buyer confirmation.
solution_plan: A plain-language Azure AI pricing explainer and cost estimator — users input their expected request volume, token usage, and gateway configuration, and the tool returns a clear monthly cost estimate with footnotes decoded into plain English, plus a comparison of tier options. The factory builds this as a Claude prompt that ingests Azure pricing page data and user inputs via a simple web form, with a Stripe payment link for a one-time report or low-price subscription ($9-$19/month). Sell by reaching cloud architects and platform engineers through Azure-specific communities (Microsoft Tech Community, LinkedIn targeting 'Azure AI' + 'platform engineer'), and via content targeting people searching for 'Azure AI Gateway pricing' — these are high-intent search queries. Delivery is fully automated: user submits config, gets estimate instantly, billed via Stripe. The only recurring human touch is updating pricing data when Azure changes its fee structure (roughly quarterly) and approving outreach. A solo non-technical operator can build and run this with the factory — but validate that engineers will pay rather than bookmark the Azure pricing page before investing.
notes: Total is exactly 5.5, just at the validate threshold. Lead reachability (4) is the weakest dimension — finding engineers actively evaluating Azure AI Gateway before they've committed is timing-sensitive. Defensibility is low (easily copyable) so speed to market matters if validated.
